title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin struck and killed a duck on a public street. A human safety operator was present in the vehicle during the incident. The vehicle was operating in autonomous mode and did not slow down or stop when it hit the animal, suggesting the system either did not detect the duck or did not classify it as an obstacle requiring avoidance.

This is a failure of perception or decision-making in a deployed autonomous system operating in a real-world environment with pedestrian and animal activity. It would have been caught by a safety operator who was empowered to override the vehicle or to decline autonomous operation in conditions where small animals were present on the roadway. Whether the safety operator could have intervened in time is not established.

Avridge confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode and stated it found no evidence the car failed to stop at a stop sign, but did not address why the system did not avoid the duck. The company has adjusted its testing area and is evaluating technology improvements through simulation.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck near Mueller Lake, prompting significant community concern about self-driving cars. A resident reported on social media that the Avride vehicle, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. The incident gained attention partly because neighbors were familiar with this particular duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant. Local residents have collected the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and stated it found no evidence supporting a resident's claim that the car failed to stop at a stop sign. The company has adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake. Avride is now evaluating technology improvements to avoid similar situations in the future through controlled simulations. The company continues testing autonomous vehicles in Austin, alongside competitors including Zoox, Tesla, and Waymo.
